<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
Sourcing this PKGBUILD for `makepkg --printsrcinfo` executes only the global/top-level scope. That scope consists entirely of standard metadata assignments: `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `depends`, `provides`, `conflicts`, the `source_x86_64` array, the `b2sums_x86_64` array, and the `package()` function definition. There are no top-level command substitutions `$(...)`, no `eval`, no `curl`/`wget`, no network calls, no obfuscated/encoded payloads, and no file operations outside ordinary variable assignment. The `package()` body (which contains only `install -Dm` commands into `$pkgdir`) is merely defined, not executed, so it is out of scope for this gate. The source URL points to the project's own GitHub release (consistent with the declared `url`), and a real b2sum is provided. Nothing in the sourced scope can execute malicious code.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Only standard metadata assignments at top level; no code execution.
</summary>
</security_assessment>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD appears legitimate and follows standard AUR packaging practices. The source downloads a prebuilt binary tarball from the project's own GitHub releases URL, which is expected upstream behavior. The b2sums checksum is set to a specific hash value (not 'SKIP'), providing integrity verification. The package() function uses only standard `install` commands to place the application's own binaries, systemd service file, sysusers configuration, and config file into appropriate system directories. There are no `eval`, `base64`, `curl|bash`, or other suspicious patterns that would indicate a supply-chain attack. No code exfiltrates data, downloads and executes arbitrary scripts, or performs unexpected system modifications. The systemd service, sysusers, and config file installations are all routine for a daemon-style application and align with the package's described purpose as a "local AI model router with a spend and quality console."
</details>
